extracted.intended_audience: DFG peer reviewers (reviewers across DFG programmes)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for evaluating research funding proposals submitted to the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG), covering the four main review criteria, reviewer obligations, and procedural quality checks across DFG programmes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of the Project
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific quality and originality of the proposed research; theoretical and methodological foundation; state of the art; innovative potential — significance of expected results for the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess originality and scientific quality, situate the project within the current state of the art, evaluate the theoretical and methodological grounding, and judge the potential significance of expected results for advancing the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives and Work Programme
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity, plausibility, and feasibility of the research objectives; coherence and adequacy of the planned work programme; realism of the timeline and milestones; appropriateness of methods to the questions; quality of preliminary work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether objectives are clearly defined and plausible, whether the work programme is coherent and adequate to reach objectives, whether timelines and milestones are realistic, whether chosen methods appropriately address the research questions, and whether preliminary work supports feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicants' Qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Track record of the applicant(s) commensurate with career stage; demonstrated expertise relevant to the proposed project; for collaborative projects: complementarity of the team; for early-career researchers: capacity for independent research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge qualifications relative to career stage and project needs, assess team complementarity for collaborations, and evaluate evidence of independence for early-career researchers. DFG explicitly requires assessment without recourse to non-scientific criteria such as age, gender, family obligations, origin, or health restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work and Research Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of necessary infrastructure (equipment, data, archives); institutional support and embedding; access to collaborators, students, networks; adequacy of requested resources to the project scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the host environment provides the facilities, institutional backing, collaborations and resources required to successfully carry out the project and whether requested resources are proportionate to the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest — Mandatory Recusal
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must decline if there is a conflict: close scientific cooperation with the applicant in the last 3 years; teacher/student/supervisor relationship; first-degree relatives or comparable personal relationship; membership in same institute/department; significant material or personal interest; direct competitive relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any listed relationship applies, the reviewer must recuse/decline. Use the specified 3-year cooperation window and consider both material and personal interests; when in doubt, follow DFG guidance and notify the office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat the proposal as confidential; do not pass it to third parties (including students or collaborators) without express DFG permission; do not exploit ideas from the proposal in own work; destroy or return copies after the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proposal materials are kept strictly confidential, seek DFG permission before sharing, avoid using any proprietary ideas from the proposal in your own research, and remove/destroy local copies after completing the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and Substantiation of the Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a written, substantiated review; justify scores with explicit reasoning tied to the four criteria; distinguish between fundamental concerns and minor remarks; avoid statements that could be construed as discriminatory; use standardised scoring (numeric scale defined per programme).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write a clear, evidence-based assessment that links judgments to the four main criteria, separate major weaknesses from minor points, refrain from discriminatory language, and apply the programme-specific numeric scoring schema while explaining the rationale for each score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond to invitations within the requested period; submit the review by the deadline; notify the office promptly if delay is unavoidable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept or decline review invitations promptly, meet submission deadlines, and proactively communicate expected delays to the DFG office to allow process management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-Stage Quality Assurance (Review Process Integrity)
rubrics_metrics.description: DFG review process includes: (1) individual reviewers producing written assessments per the four criteria; (2) review boards (elected discipline-specific committees) that synthesise reviews and rank proposals; (3) Joint Committee making final funding decisions considering programme balance and discipline strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that individual reviews feed into panel synthesis and final committee decisions; reviewers should aim for clarity and consistency because their written assessments will be used in ranking and allocation deliberations and may be scrutinised at higher decision levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent Quality Check (Procedural and Ethical Compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: A separate Quality and Programme Management unit checks every review process for procedural compliance, applicant eligibility verification, review consistency across panels, ethics-approval verification, and detection of potentially discriminatory language in reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that reviews are subject to independent checks for both procedural correctness and content standards (e.g., discriminatory language, ethics approvals). Ensure reviews are compliant, substantiated, and free of inappropriate wording to pass these quality checks.
